tagline: Specs as a verified, queryable decision database.
keyFeatures: Specs are typed database entities — decisions, acceptance criteria, tasks — edited live by humans (web UI) and agents (MCP), not markdown files
draft → specify → build → verify → done pipeline; each acceptance criterion gates on real test-run evidence with human sign-off to close
Standards (codified cross-cutting rules) with drift detection: spec ↔ spec, spec ↔ standards, code ↔ standards
Knowledge graph across specs with semantic + graph retrieval (pgvector) — 'the unit of retrieval is the relevant fact, not the document'
Self-hostable TypeScript/Hono/Postgres stack or hosted SaaS; Claude-powered agent embedded in every spec
limitations: Earliest-stage commercial entrant tracked: no tagged releases, 29★ / 0 forks, ~5 contributors incl. the CEO
Specs live in an external database, not the repo — real-time collaboration traded for git-native diffs, offline access, and a new spec ↔ repo sync surface
Fair-code, not OSI open source; enterprise `.ee.` features separately licensed; pricing not publicly verifiable at review time
Claude-centric: only Claude Code/Desktop documented as MCP clients
Requires server + PostgreSQL 16 (or SaaS) — heaviest infrastructure footprint in the tracked set for solo use
